mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q01.stem: A comparison table shows general surface-treatment thickness ranges. How should they be used?
options: Adopt them directly as every product's acceptance range.
The maximum gives the best value of every property.
Use them as comparison guides and separately check product specifications and applicability.
Omit substrate checks.
reasons: A general range is not an individual product's acceptance criterion.
Thickness alone cannot guarantee every optimum property.
Separate comparison guides from requirements and applicability.
Substrate is important in method selection.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q02.stem: The material changed but the process sheet still names the old material. What is appropriate?
options: Start from past success with the old material alone.
Ask about pretreatment, underlayers and inspection effects; identify items as awaiting confirmation.
Thicken the main coating to eliminate checks.
Change the material name back to the old one.
reasons: Old-material success does not guarantee new-material compatibility.
Identify and hold until substrate-change effects are confirmed.
Thicker coating cannot replace pretreatment or material compatibility.
Do not rewrite a material name contrary to reality.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q03.stem: Which statement about a hot-dip interface alloy layer is appropriate?
options: It always has the same thickness in every method.
It has no dimensional effect.
It is identical despite different materials and processes.
Check the substrate/bath combination and conditions together with required dimensions.
reasons: The layer changes with combinations and process conditions.
Layers and thickness can affect fits and dimensions.
Different materials or treatments need not produce the same layer.
Check substrate, bath, conditions and required dimensions together.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q04.stem: You need to distinguish a small hole reaching the substrate from a coating depression that does not. What is appropriate?
options: Treat the former as a pinhole and the latter as a pit, confirming by the prescribed method.
Call everything a blister without checking depth.
Accept every shallow defect unconditionally.
Enlarge the hole with a needle to check.
reasons: Separate the categories and confirm by the prescribed method.
A blister separates from the substrate; it is not a name for every hole.
Depth alone does not determine acceptance for each product.
Unauthorized enlargement changes the original condition.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q05.stem: A hairline-specified item develops strong mirror gloss. What is appropriate?
options: It is always acceptable because it is shiniest.
Line direction is irrelevant.
Compare the appearance sample, line direction and inspection conditions, then request a decision.
Rename the process mirror finishing.
reasons: The required finish need not be mirror.
Specified line direction can be part of hairline requirements.
Request a decision using samples, direction and inspection conditions.
Do not remove requirements by unauthorized process renaming.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q06.stem: Only the edge coating repeatedly peels after polishing. What is appropriate?
options: Hide it by unauthorized polishing.
Increasing speed always fixes it.
Mix with good items and ship.
Record location, holding and contact angle, then send for designated evaluation.
reasons: Hiding a defect does not confirm suitability or cause.
Higher speed can create other defects such as heating.
Separate suspected nonconforming items from good stock.
Record conditions and send for approved evaluation.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q07.stem: A thickness gauge is nondestructive. Which understanding is appropriate?
options: Even a low-sample-damage category still requires compatibility and equipment safety controls.
There is absolutely no human hazard.
It suits every substrate and coating.
Calibration can be omitted forever.
reasons: Manage sample-damage classification separately from safety and compatibility.
Even nondestructive X-ray methods can require dedicated controls.
Principles have substrate, coating and shape applicability limits.
Calibration and reference-sample checks remain necessary.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q08.stem: What is appropriate about metal films on resin?
options: They can never be applied to nonmetals.
Methods exist that require suitable materials and pretreatment.
Put every resin into the same bath.
No pretreatment is ever needed.
reasons: Methods exist for metal films on nonmetal substrates.
Check material and required pretreatment/catalyst compatibility.
Resin type and process conditions need checking.
Nonconductive substrates still require appropriate pretreatment.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q09.stem: A process sheet changes from zinc-based to aluminium-based. What is appropriate?
options: Immersion means all conditions are identical.
Use the old bath if the color is similar.
Apply the old temperature without checking.
Compare substrate, process number, performance and dimensions.
reasons: Different bath materials can require different conditions.
Color does not prove compatibility or required performance.
Do not transfer the old temperature without conditions.
Compare specified material, process number and performance/dimensions.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q10.stem: An edge has an excess hot-dip metal projection. What is appropriate?
options: Record location and dimensions, identify it and request a specification-based decision.
Leave every case because the textbook says effects are small.
Grind it off without approval and accept it.
Declare there is always one cause.
reasons: Preserve run location, dimensions and history, then judge by requirements.
A general explanation cannot authorize leaving every product.
Grinding changes dimensions or coating and requires approval.
Appearance alone does not establish a single cause.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q11.stem: Which statement about grit numbers and surface roughness is correct?
options: They are the same physical quantity.
Every product system's grit numbers are universally identical.
Grit indicates fineness and is treated separately from measured roughness.
Matching grit gives identical results on every material.
reasons: Grit and roughness are different quantities.
Do not unconditionally equate different numbering systems.
Grit indicates particle or similar fineness, distinct from measured roughness.
Material and condition also change results.

mfg1-surface-weekly-09-q12.stem: When deriving thickness from mass difference before and after stripping, what else is needed?
options: Only container color.
Area, density and removal conditions.
Only operator preference.
Only the weekday.
reasons: Color provides no mass-to-thickness conversion basis.
Area, density and removal suitability are conversion prerequisites.
Preference is not a measurement conversion basis.
Weekday is not a required physical quantity.
